description: Add a zero-dependency static HTML page explaining the 8 planets of our solar system

userStories.title: Define planet data as HTML content
userStories.description: As a developer exploring this project, I want all 8 solar system planets documented with key facts so that the page content is accurate and educational
acceptanceCriteria: All 8 planets are present: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Each planet entry includes at minimum: name, planet type (terrestrial/gas giant/ice giant), distance from Sun, and one notable characteristic
Content is authored as semantic HTML markup (headings + lists or definition lists) — no JavaScript data structures
No external data sources, APIs, or CDN dependencies are referenced
`src/index.js` is not touched — `node src/index.js` still outputs exactly `Hello, AI Coding Agent!\n`
userStories.technicalNotes: Content lives directly in `planets.html` at project root. No JavaScript. Use `<section>` or `<article>` per planet, `<h2>` for planet names, `<ul>` or `<dl>` for facts. Project root placement avoids violating the single-file `src/` architecture rule defined in CLAUDE.md and MISSION.md.
userStories.notes: ⚠️ Requires human authorisation — scope expansion beyond current MISSION.md boundaries. Do not implement without explicit human PR approval.

userStories.title: Create styled planets.html static page
userStories.description: As a user opening the project directory, I want to open planets.html in a browser and see a readable, styled page about the solar system so that I can learn about planets without needing a server
acceptanceCriteria: `planets.html` exists at project root (not under `src/`)
File opens in a browser via `open planets.html` (or double-click) with zero JavaScript console errors
Page has a `<title>` of 'Planets of Our Solar System'
Inline `<style>` block present — no `<link rel=stylesheet>`, no CDN, no external resources
All 8 planet sections render correctly with content from US-001
Page is readable with JavaScript disabled (zero `<script>` tags)
`npm run lint` still exits 0 after file is added
`npm run type-check` still exits 0 after file is added
No `package-lock.json` generated
userStories.technicalNotes: File: `./planets.html` (project root). Inline CSS only — background, font-family (system stack), headings, planet cards or sections. Follow lowercase filename convention from CLAUDE.md. `node --check` does not scan `.html` files so no lint impact. `.gitignore` does not exclude `.html` at root so no gitignore changes needed.

userStories.title: Validate governance gates post-addition
userStories.description: As a project maintainer, I want all existing quality gates to still pass after planets.html is added so that the benchmark instrument remains fully intact
acceptanceCriteria: `node src/index.js` outputs exactly `Hello, AI Coding Agent!\n` — byte-exact, verified with `node src/index.js | xxd`
`npm run lint` exits 0 with no output
`npm run type-check` exits 0 with no output
`npm test` exits 0 (note: silent exit 0 is acceptable here only because no new `.test.js` file is being added — the false-pass state is pre-existing)
No `package-lock.json` exists in the repository
`src/index.js` is unchanged — blank line between `}` and `main();` is present, ES5 syntax only, trailing newline present
`planets.html` has no references to `src/index.js` or any JS runtime
Protected files untouched: MISSION.md, GUARDRAILS.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, .gitignore, package.json
userStories.technicalNotes: Run full pre-PR gate from CLAUDE.md: `npm run lint && npm run type-check && npm test`. Then manually run `node src/index.js | xxd` and verify byte output. Inspect `src/index.js` manually for blank line and ES5 compliance. Confirm no lockfile with `ls package-lock.json 2>&1`.
userStories.notes: This story is a validation/QA story — it produces no new files, only runs checks.
